deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for the introductory, function-theoretic part of Riemann's theory of linear differential equations with algebraic coefficients. The surrounding pages count constants and determine the form of the differential equation from a given branching class. This page sets up the notions that the theory needs.

(0) Top lines, heavily corrected. With the help of a 'latter corollary', Riemann announces a general expression for all solutions. From it one should see at once that the totality of solutions of the system above is represented by it, and conversely. The page is too damaged here for any mathematics to be reconstructed.

(1) Uniqueness of analytic continuation. A function of x+yi given on some part of the z-plane can be continued beyond it continuously in only one way. Here 'continuously' means: satisfying the partial differential equation i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y, which is the complex form of the Cauchy–Riemann equations.

Check (mine): if w = f(x+iy) with f holomorphic, then ∂w/∂x = f' and ∂w/∂y = i f'. Hence ∂w/∂y = i ∂w/∂x, as written.

Riemann then states his programme. The functions to be studied are not defined by analytic expressions or equations in z. Instead, their value is given on an arbitrary bounded part of the z-plane, and they are continued from there while satisfying the PDE.

The continuation must proceed through strips of finite width, not along mere lines. Along a line the partial differential equation could not be applied. Under this proviso the continuation is completely determined.

(2) Single- vs many-valued. Depending on the function, continuation along any path may always return the same value at the same z. In that case the function is called 'einwerthig' (single-valued): a completely determined function of z that is not discontinuous along any line. Otherwise it is 'mehrwerthig' (many-valued).

(3) Branch points. For a many-valued function one has above all certain points of the z-plane around which the function continues into another value.

Example: f = (z−a)^μ with μ not an integer, at the point a. Draw any line (a cut) from a. One can choose the function near a so that it varies continuously everywhere off this line. On the two sides of the line it takes different values, the ratio being e^{2μπi}.

Derivation (mine): write (z−a)^μ = exp(μ log(z−a)). A positive circuit around a adds 2πi to the logarithm, so the function is multiplied by e^{2μπi}. So the continuation across the cut onto one side gives e^{2μπi} times the value already there.

(4) Definitions. The various continuations of a function over one and the same part of the plane are called its branches ('Zweige'). A point around which one branch continues into another is called a branch point ('Verzweigungspunkt').

For the investigation it is convenient to fix such cuts. Continuing across a cut from one side to the other then gives, in the region beyond, a function different from the one already there: in the example, everywhere e^{2μπi} times as large.

(5) Orientation convention. Riemann refers to Gauss's name 'positive lateral unit' for +i. He defines the positive direction of rotation relative to a given direction as the one that stands to it as +i stands to 1, i.e. counterclockwise. This fixes the sense of the circuits defining the monodromy multipliers.
errors: No mathematical errors. The CR equation i w_x = w_y is correct for holomorphic w(x+iy).

Which side of the cut carries the factor e^{2μπi} rather than e^{-2μπi} depends on the orientation convention. That convention is fixed only at the bottom of the page, so the draft is momentarily ambiguous; this is not an error.
The claim that continuation along finite-width strips is 'completely determined' is the identity theorem. It is stated without proof here and appeals to 'the preceding'.

results.what: Uniqueness of continuation of a function of x+iy satisfying i∂w/∂x=∂w/∂y from a region of the plane
results.modern_name: Identity theorem / uniqueness of analytic continuation
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851 dissertation) and Weierstrass; Cauchy for the underlying power-series theory

results.what: Defining functions by their values on a region plus continuation, rather than by formulas; single-valued vs many-valued; branches and branch points; (z−a)^μ example with multiplier e^{2μπi}
results.modern_name: Analytic continuation, branches, branch points, local monodromy
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851 dissertation; 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'; 1857 hypergeometric paper; posthumous 'Zwei allgemeine Sätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten')

results.what: Positive rotation direction defined via +i relative to 1, following Gauss's 'positive laterale Einheit'
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1831, Anzeige of Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum II) for the terminology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known introductory passage of Riemann's posthumously published fragment on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients (Werke, 1876). Its content — analytic continuation, branches, branch points, the monodromy of (z−a)^μ, the Gauss orientation convention — is standard and already firmly attributed to Riemann. Only the drafting variants are of interest.

checkable.asserts: (x+iy)^mu satisfies Riemann's form i w_x = w_y of the Cauchy-Riemann equations (result 0)
Any holomorphic function, e.g. exp, satisfies i w_x = w_y (result 0)
One positive circuit around a multiplies (z-a)^mu = exp(mu*log(z-a)) by exp(2*pi*I*mu)
For integer mu the multiplier is 1, so a is not a branch point (result 1)

transcription_corrections: '(der Gestalt dass sie i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y genügt)' is better read as a parenthetical about the partial differential equation i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y being satisfied during continuation. The later line '(wo bei einer Fortsetzung ... eine partielle Differentialgleichung nicht zur Anwendung kommen könnte)' confirms this.

'Ein solcher Punkt ist z.B. bei der Function (z−a)^μ, wenn μ keine ganze Zahl ist, der Punkt a' is consistent with the image; the following 'Denkt man sich vom Punkte a aus eine beliebige Linie gezogen' is likewise.
'auf der gestrichenen [?]' at the end of the e^{2μπi} sentence is uncertain. Context (one side of the cut vs the other) suggests something like 'auf der negativen' or 'auf der anderen' Seite.

'Werth, um welchen herum sich ein Zweig ... fortsetzt' likely begins 'Ein Punkt/Werth' (the first word is struck). The term defined is 'Verzweigungspunkt' (possibly 'Verzweigungswerth'); the image is ambiguous.
Bottom: 'die von Gauss vorgeschlagene Benennung positive laterale Einheit für +i' — the insertion above reads 'vorgeschlagen wurde', forming a corrected version of the same clause.
